growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two oval cotyledons, then pairs of small, short, rounded-oval leaves, much less narrow than the adult's. The young wild olive is a dense, twiggy, often spiny shrub of many stems with tiny leaves (a browse-resistant juvenile form) for years; eventually one or a few stems grow out into a tree with narrow, grey-green, silver-backed leaves and a gnarled, fissured, hollowing trunk.
growth.source: Olive horticulture and oleaster ecology: long juvenile phase (seedlings fruit after ~8-15 yr), juvenile foliage small and rounded with spiny shoots; seed with hard endocarp germinates slowly (1-6 months after removal of the stone); trees live many centuries, some over 2000 yr (Wikipedia Olive; Rey & Alcantara 2000 on oleaster recruitment)

fruiting.source: Olive crop literature (Lavee; FAO/IOC): small creamy 4-lobed flowers in axillary racemes of 10-40 in spring, mainly wind pollinated, only ~1-2% of flowers set fruit; fruit green turning purple-black in autumn-winter, ~5-7 months after bloom; wild oleaster fruit small (~1-1.5 cm); bitter until cured

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the acorn stays buried and roots deeply before a thin shoot appears. Seedlings and saplings carry holly-like leaves with spiny teeth, dark glossy green above and grey-felted below; adult leaves are smaller, entire and leathery. Young plants grow slowly in the shade of shrubs and trees, often bushy from browsing, before a single stem leads.
growth.source: European Atlas of Forest Tree Species (Quercus ilex: to 25 m, rarely 30; lifespan may exceed 1000 yr; shade-tolerant, regenerates under canopy); Wikipedia (young trees spiny-toothed, adults entire; Encina Tres Patas ~1,200 yr); growth rate and first-acorn age estimated

fruiting.source: European Atlas of Forest Tree Species (flowers May-Jun with new leaves; acorns ripen the first year, brown, 1.5-2 cm, a third to half in a light green cup; fall Nov-Jan; big crops every 4-6 yr); Wikipedia (1-3 acorns on a short stalk); sweet acorns of subsp. rotundifolia are eaten raw or roasted

canopy.name: Mediterranean cypress

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal, with slender cotyledons; the first shoots bear small, spreading needle-like juvenile leaves before the dark green, appressed scale leaves take over. Fast-growing when young: a dense, narrow cone of upswept branches (a slim column in the fastigiate form, which is what most planted trees are; wild trees spread horizontally).
growth.source: conifers.org (20-30 m, fast-growing when young, seeds from its tenth year, up to 1000 yr; cones 2-3 cm, 8-14 scales, serotinous); Wikipedia (to 35 m, >1000 yr, Sarv-e Abarkuh estimated ~4000 yr); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual (cones ripen second year, 64-280 seeds, 28-d germination test)

The bark turns red-brown and shreddy.

ground.name: Wall moss

growth.juvenile_note: Spores sprout into a green protonemal web in mortar joints and on brick or stone within weeks, soon budding tiny upright shoots. Cushions are small, dense and greyish-green, under 1 cm tall, of tongue-shaped leaves tipped with long silvery hair points that make them look hoary, and are soon topped by many upright cylindrical capsules on 0.6-1.5 cm stalks.
growth.source: Wikipedia Tortula muralis (greyish-green cushions to 1 cm tall, hair-pointed leaves, seta 0.6-1.5 cm, urn 1.5-2.7 mm, autoicous, cosmopolitan on walls, concrete, rocks and soil). Capsules are produced abundantly; spore-to-cushion time, spread and cushion age estimated from moss biology.

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

ground.name: Bracken

growth.juvenile_note: Young plants appear 6-7 weeks after spores land on burnt or disturbed bare soil: the first fronds are small, simple and lobed, becoming finely divided and adult-like after about 18 weeks. After up to 10 fronds a rhizome starts, which may grow 2 m in the first year; by year two the patch can be about 2 m across, sending up single, triangular, much-divided fronds from underground.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Pteridium aquilinum (young plants 6-7 weeks after spores shed; adult-like fronds after 18 weeks; rhizome to 217 cm in year 1; spores usually in the 3rd-4th season; cover under 5% below 25% of full sun); Wikipedia (individual rhizomes live up to 72 yr; colonies 650 to over 1,400 yr old).

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

epiphyte.source: Evernia prunastri, Parmeliaceae: oakmoss, a shrubby lichen of strap-like antler-branched lobes 3-8 cm, grey-green above and white beneath, hanging from the twigs of oaks and other trees across Europe and the Mediterranean; harvested in the Balkans and Morocco for perfume — Index Fungorum; British Lichen Society; Brodo, Lichens of North America

leaf.notes: flat strap-like branches forked like antlers, grey-green above and white below, dusted with soredia

appearance.seasonal: softer and greener when wet, brittle grey when dry
appearance.silhouette: soft grey-green antler tufts hanging from oak twigs
appearance.refs: British Lichen Society; Brodo et al., Lichens of North America; Index Fungorum

epiphyte.silhouette: soft grey-green antler tufts hanging from oak twigs

associations.name: Holm oak sclerophyll forest
associations.where: deep-soil valleys and shaded north slopes of the Mediterranean basin
associations.source: Quezel & Medail 2003 Ecologie et biogeographie des forets du bassin mediterraneen; Braun-Blanquet Quercetum ilicis

associations.name: Cork oak-wild olive open woodland
associations.where: acid sandy lowlands and warm sunny lower slopes, thin soil
associations.source: Rivas-Martinez 1987 Memoria del mapa de series de vegetacion de Espana; Quezel & Medail 2003

associations.name: Aleppo pine-kermes oak garrigue
associations.where: hot dry limestone hillsides and rocky ridges, frequently burned
associations.source: Tomaselli 1977 Degradation of the Mediterranean maquis (UNESCO MAB); Quezel & Medail 2003

associations.name: Coast live oak-chaparral mosaic
associations.where: canyon bottoms and north slopes of the California coast ranges, oak grove with chaparral on hot exposed slopes
associations.source: Barbour & Major 1977 Terrestrial Vegetation of California; Sawyer, Keeler-Wolf & Evens 2009 Manual of California Vegetation

associations.name: Proteoid fynbos
associations.where: wet sandy south-facing mountain slopes of the Cape, nutrient-poor soil, fire every 10-20 years
associations.source: Cowling 1992 The Ecology of Fynbos; Mucina & Rutherford 2006 Vegetation of South Africa

associations.name: Andean dry montane scrub
associations.where: warmer dry inter-Andean valleys and canyon sides, about 1,500-2,800 m
associations.source: Inter-Andean dry valleys and rocky slopes of Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia (about 1,500-3,400 m): columnar cacti — Trichocereus (Echinopsis), with Browningia and Armatocereus lower down — among Puya, Agave, Opuntia, Dodonaea and Schinus molle; seasonally dry montane scrub (Weberbauer 1945; Ostolaza 2014 Cactaceae of Peru; Josse et al. 2009, NatureServe ecological systems of the Andes).
associations._note: 1 Oct (Mike: Trichocereus must be in the game): the realm gate only lets an 'andes' species grow in a biome that hosts the andes realm, and no dry biome did (only cold puna and paramo), so no Trichocereus could grow on any planet. The trim fills the companions and ground with real inter-Andean species.
